nm_los_alamos_crags.blurb: Los Alamos Crags gathers climbing in the canyons and outcrops around the town of Los Alamos, New Mexico. The rock changes with the place. Pueblo Canyon, running through the middle of town, is a tuff canyon known for streambed bouldering and some longer cracks on variable rock. The Mitchell Trail crags northwest of town are rhyolite, a short hike from the trailhead. Los Alamos Canyon has sport routes on rhyolite and tuff, and its south side is best known for ice. Sport and bouldering are the main styles, with some trad, ice and a little mixed climbing. Sport grades are mostly 5.9 to 5.12, boulder problems run V0 to V7, and the ice reaches WI4.

or_west_side.blurb: West Side is the west bank of the Lower Gorge at Smith Rock in central Oregon, a run of basalt columns on the rimrock above the river. The Lower Gorge as a whole is known for cracks, and the climbing here is mostly trad with a good number of harder sport routes. Most climbs fall roughly between 5.10 and 5.12. The walls stay in shade for nearly the whole day. Catwalk Cliff and Wildfire Wall hold the most climbs, with Star Wall, Jungle Land and Parched Cat Cliff making up the rest of the five crags.

qc_mont_rigaud.blurb: Mont Rigaud is a sport crag in Quebec's Montérégie, west of Montreal near the Ontario border and about 45 minutes out of the city. The rock is pink granite, with walls roughly 10 to 15 metres tall. Bolted routes make up most of the climbing, alongside some trad, a few top-ropes and about a dozen boulder problems. Grades run from easy to 5.12, mostly 5.8 to 5.11. Sun reaches the cliff from late morning into early afternoon, and scattered trees shade it in summer. STD Wall, Gully Walls and Main Wall hold the most climbs: Main Wall has good moderates, Gully Walls is easy to top-rope, and STD Wall is the steepest, with some of the hardest lines.

ri_rocky_point.blurb: Rocky Point is a bouldering area in Warwick, Rhode Island, on the grounds of a former amusement park that is now a state park. Nearly all of it is bouldering, with a single top-rope line. Some of the boulders have overhangs and caves, notably around Caves and Troll Toll. Railroad Area holds the most climbs, with Caves and Troll Toll and Puddingstone Heights close behind, and a scatter of smaller groups through the park. Problems run from V0 to V10, with the bulk between V0 and V4 and a handful of hard ones at the top. Puddingstone Heights is a newer zone whose boulders still need cleaning.

sd_south_seas.blurb: South Seas is a sport-climbing area in the Black Hills of South Dakota, a few miles from the Mount Rushmore faces. The rock is granite, climbed on spires and small crystalline walls, and most routes end on top of a spire, so the way down is a rappel. Sport dominates, with some trad and a few boulder problems at South Seas Boulders. The routes are moderate and well bolted, mostly 5.6 to 5.12 with the most in the 5.8 to 5.11 range. Hornets Nest holds the most climbs, followed by Shipyard Rock and Bull Rock, among two dozen sub-areas. No approach runs longer than about 30 minutes, and the area is described as a good place to start sampling Rushmore climbing.

tx_rogers_park.blurb: Rogers Park is a limestone bouldering area above Belton Lake in central Texas, near Belton and about an hour north of Austin. A cliff band holds walls roughly 12 to 30 feet high, with pocketed climbing, and the problems get sun and shade though mostly shade. Everything here is bouldering, split across about twenty small walls and caves. Billiards Wall holds the most climbs, followed by The Pit, Little Cave, Hog's Back Caves and Little New Wall. Grades run from V0 to V11, with most of the problems between V0 and V5 and a smaller group of hard ones above that.
